engineSummary: A three-input engine. Only sex, the woman's age band (under 50 or 50+) and the topical/oral preference reach the recommendation call, which runs before any medical question. Men and women 50+ get dutasteride + minoxidil; women under 50 get minoxidil topical + a spironolactone/minoxidil capsule. The topical + capsule "Dual" bundle is always first and pre-selected; the second card is Topical (or SuperCapsule if the person said Oral). After the choice, about 12 to 16 medical questions follow. They add follow-up pages (free text, reactions, partner-pregnancy consent, three blood-pressure questions for capsule plans) but never remove, switch or block a product: 25 live one-change tests (21 in stage 2, 4 more in the stage 3 check) changed the offer only through sex/age band and method. Answers are tagged important or critical for a dermatologist who reviews after checkout. The only hard stop is age under 18, and a woman whose birth date does not fit her band is sent back to choose again. The email wall is a split test: in one arm it comes before the recommendation screen.
strengths: Very short path to a named plan: six profile questions, then a clear two-card choice with a "best for" line on each.
Leads with dutasteride and 8% minoxidil, stronger than most rivals' first offer, and explains each ingredient.
A clear age rule for women: no finasteride or dutasteride for women who say they are under 50, and a date-of-birth check that sends a mismatched woman back.
Branching follow-ups capture detail where it matters (free text for symptoms, conditions, other patterns, reactions; a written partner-pregnancy consent).
Asks blood pressure, weight and last check-up only when an oral capsule is chosen, keeping the topical path short.
A customisation box lets the patient ask the doctor to change the formula.
weaknesses: The product is chosen before any safety question, and the most intensive plan (dutasteride + oral minoxidil) is pre-selected for every man, even "just exploring" or "prevention only".
Red flags do nothing on screen: bald patches, severe scalp symptoms ("may disqualify you"), heart disease with oral minoxidil, a reaction to finasteride, all leave the plan unchanged.
A pregnant partner who declines finasteride/dutasteride still has dutasteride in the plan; a woman 50+ who can become pregnant is offered dutasteride with no warning.
Goal, duration, family history and hair-loss pattern are asked "to personalise" but change nothing.
Age comes from a self-chosen band; the real birth date is asked only at the end and does not change the product. No upper age limit.
No price on the recommendation screen; price appears only after email and mobile number.
Finasteride, the usual first-line drug, is never offered by the assessment.
opportunities: Ask safety questions first and let them shape the offer: remove oral minoxidil for heart disease or low blood pressure, drop 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors when the patient declines them, refer patchy loss or scarring signs.
Use goal, pattern and duration to offer a gentler start (topical only, finasteride) to "prevention" or "exploring" patients.
Offer finasteride as first line with a plain comparison against dutasteride.
Show the price on the recommendation screen before asking for contact details.
Use the actual date of birth (not a band) and handle older adults and post-menopausal women under 50 explicitly.
Ask about women's specific causes (iron, thyroid, PCOS, recent childbirth or illness), which this quiz does not ask.

verification.verdict: The core finding holds up well. Every high-impact rule re-tested live (stops, product family by sex and age band, card swap by method, topical-only skipping the blood-pressure questions, medical answers never changing the plan) reproduced exactly, and the served code agrees. The one real error was the account wall: it is a split test, and in one arm it comes before the recommendation is shown. Facts about the six products the quiz returns are reliable (live API data). Facts about the rest of the catalogue are weaker: they rest on help-centre text, third-party reviews and search summaries because the marketing site's robots.txt bars this agent, and one stage 2 price was out of date. Treat the engine logic as high confidence and the wider catalogue prices as rough.
